```python
from typing import List

def is_valid_sudoku(board: List[List[str]]) -> bool:
    rows = [set() for _ in range(9)]
    cols = [set() for _ in range(9)]
    boxes = [[set() for _ in range(3)] for _ in range(3)]

    for i in range(9):
        for j in range(9):
            num = board[i][j]
            if num == '.':
                continue
            if num in rows[i] or num in cols[j] or num in boxes[i // 3][j // 3]:
                return False
            rows[i].add(num)
            cols[j].add(num)
            boxes[i // 3][j // 3].add(num)

    return True
```

This function checks each row, column, and 3x3 sub-box for duplicates, ignoring empty cells. It uses sets to track seen numbers efficiently. The time complexity is O(1) since the board size is fixed at 9x9, and the space complexity is also O(1) due to the constant-sized data structures used.
